requirements.text: log today's outage for me ... all SAP users are unable to connect ... production-wide SAP outage ... reported this morning by phone
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_001' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND status = 'new' AND channel = 'phone'
requirements.source: Outage Incident Created (High Impact/Urgency) And Linked To CI
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100)
caller is Thomas Green = USER_001 on the seed; the check's description says USER_004 but its query says USER_001, and USER_004 is the acting user Joanne Simpson, so the query stands
CI with serial SRV-ORC-9981 is CI_001 (SAP-DB-01 (Oracle Database), status in_use, so linkable under policy 5.1)
impact and urgency high from policy 3.1: 'production-wide' and 'all users' outages are high/high; priority critical from the matrix
status new is the policy 3.1 default
channel phone from 'reported this morning by phone', added beyond the benchmark check's cells
opened_by is not tested on the incident: neither pass tested it and the merge adds nothing neither pass found

requirements.text: ensure it is clearly associated with the SAP database server involved
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_affected_cis_id = 'TASKCI_015' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND incident_id = 'INC_101'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (TASKCI_015 after TASKCI_014); the incident id INC_101 is also assumed next in sequence

the association is the affected-CI link (link_affected_ci_to_incident is listed) as well as the incident's configuration_item cell; the benchmark check selects by CI only (the seed has no row for CI_001)

requirements.text: log today's outage (not assigned: the request names no assignee)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_001' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND assigned_to IS NULL
assumptions: assigned_to IS NULL kept from the benchmark check; the request names no assignee or group and no assignment tool is listed
id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100)

requirements.text: register this SAP database instability as an ongoing underlying issue so future SAP outages on the same server can be correlated
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_011' AND configuration_item = 'CI_001' AND opened_by = 'USER_004' AND status = 'new' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (PRB_011 after PRB_010)
a new problem row, not an update of PRB_001 (the seed's SAP Oracle problem on CI_001, status fix_in_progress): the request says register, and no listed tool updates a problem
'the same server' is CI_001, so configuration_item = CI_001

disagreement: opened_by: A untested, B USER_004; chose USER_004 because problem.opened_by is NOT NULL in the schema and policy 3.1 defines opened_by as the user submitting, which is the acting user Joanne Simpson (USER_004); Thomas Green (USER_001) reported the outage but has no column in problem
status new is the policy 4.2 default

impact high, urgency high and priority critical kept from the benchmark check; the request fixes none of them for the problem, though its production-wide wording matches policy 3.1's high/high rule and the 4.2 matrix gives critical

requirements.text: ensure it is clearly associated with the SAP database server involved (boundary: the SAP application server is not linked)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE configuration_item = 'CI_002'
assumptions: boundary of the CI selector: CI_002 (SAP-APP-01 (Application Server), serial SRV-LNX-4421) is the near match a loose reading of 'SAP database server' could link; the request names the database server by serial SRV-ORC-9981 (CI_001); the seed's one link for CI_002 (TASKCI_001, INC_001) must stay the only one

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the incident INC_101 (caller USER_001, CI_001, high/high/critical, new, phone), the affected-CI link TASKCI_015, the unassigned check, the new problem PRB_011 on CI_001 (new, high/high/critical) and all four dispositions (kept).
disagreement: value: problem.opened_by: A leaves it untested, B tests USER_004; chose USER_004 (the tighter predicate) because the column is NOT NULL and policy 3.1 defines opened_by as the user submitting, which is the acting user Joanne Simpson; Thomas Green only reported the outage and problem has no caller column.
disagreement: missing requirement: A adds a stay that the SAP application server CI_002 gains no affected-CI link (configuration_item = 'CI_002', expected 1, the seed's TASKCI_001); B has none; kept because it is the boundary of the CI selector: a loose reading of 'the SAP database server' would link the other SAP server, while the request fixes the CI by serial SRV-ORC-9981.
The second and fourth checks' descriptions say the caller is USER_004 but their queries say USER_001; the seed makes Thomas Green USER_001 and USER_004 the acting user, so the queries stand and only the descriptions are wrong. Policy 4.2 says a problem must link its affected incidents via an incident_to_problem related list, but the schema has no such table and the candidate columns (incident.problem, problem.original_task) are named by neither request nor policy, so no linking requirement is written; an agent that sets them breaks nothing here. Policy 7 (knowledge search and suggested links on incident creation) has no search or link tool in the task's list and fixes no article, so it is not a requirement. The first check's name ends in a trailing space and is keyed exactly as given.
